executive_summary.content: The Customer Support Portal project aims to reduce customer support call volume and enhance customer experience by providing an online platform. This portal will empower customers to self-manage simple support requests, track ticket statuses, and submit new tickets, thereby streamlining support operations and improving customer satisfaction.

project_overview.description: An online portal allowing customers to handle simple status updates and ticket requests themselves to reduce the volume of customer support calls.

objectives: Reduce support workload while improving customer experience by allowing customers to track their own requests online instead of calling.

in_scope: Customer registration, login, and password reset via email.
Customers creating and tracking support tickets.
Email notifications for customers on ticket status changes.
Customers uploading screenshots or PDF documents with tickets.
Customers searching for previously submitted tickets by ticket number.
Customers editing tickets only when the ticket status is 'Open'.
Support agent dashboard for viewing, updating, assigning, and reassigning tickets.
Support agents adding internal notes to tickets.
Support agents searching tickets by number, customer email, and priority.
Basic reporting for MVP (number of open tickets, average resolution time, tickets by priority).
out_of_scope: Mobile application development (planned for Phase two)

requirements: Customers must be able to independently manage their support requests and track ticket statuses online.
The system must facilitate a reduction in the volume of direct customer support calls.
The portal must enhance customer satisfaction through efficient self-service capabilities.
Support staff require efficient tools to manage and resolve customer issues effectively.
Customers should be able to register using their email address.
Registered customers should be able to securely log in.
Customers should be able to reset forgotten passwords via email.
Customers should be able to create and track support tickets.
Customers should receive email notifications whenever the status of a ticket changes.
Support agents should have a dedicated dashboard to view all assigned tickets, update ticket status, and assign or reassign tickets to other agents.
Support agents should be able to add internal notes that remain hidden from customers.
Customers should be able to upload screenshots or PDF documents when submitting a ticket.
Customers should be able to search for previously submitted tickets using the ticket number.
Customers should be able to edit tickets only while the ticket is still Open (before it moves to In Progress).
Support agents should be able to search tickets by ticket number, customer email, and priority.
The system should provide basic reporting for MVP including number of open tickets, average resolution time, and tickets by priority.
Customer passwords must never be stored in plain text and should be securely hashed.
All customer information should be encrypted while stored in the database.
Support agents and administrators should authenticate using multi-factor authentication.
User sessions should automatically expire after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Only support agents and administrators should be able to access internal ticket notes.
All important user actions should be recorded in audit logs for compliance purposes.
Availability target: Ninety-nine point nine percent.
Estimated around five thousand concurrent users.
Average response time should stay below five hundred milliseconds.
Daily database backups.

decisions: Customer accounts will use email and password for the first release; MFA for customers can wait.
Social login is marked as a future enhancement and not for MVP.
Editing of tickets is restricted to before the ticket moves to 'In Progress' status.

questions: Should customers be allowed to reopen closed tickets?
What is the max attachment size?
